The present DAR (Detailed Accident Report) for compensation relates to grievous injury suffered by the claimant Sh. Anand Kumar in a road accident that took place on 29.05.2018 at about 4:45 p.m., on C. Hexagon, India Gate in front of Princess Park, New Delhi, regarding which one FIR No.76/2018, U/s 279/338 IPC was registered at PS Tilak Marg.

The vehicle involved in this case is a car bearing registration No. DL1ZB5532, which at the relevant time of accident was being driven by respondent no 1 Sh. Pintu Kumar Pandit and owned by respondent no. 2 Sh. Jitendra Prasad.

sentences.text: Brief facts of the case that on 09.05.2018, SI Ichha Ram alongwith Ct. Surender after receiving DD No. 6A, reached the spot i.e. C. Hexagon, India Gate near Copernius Mark Princess Park, New Delhi where found accidental scooty bearing no. DL1S AA-9895 and car bearing no. DL 1ZB-5532.

The injured found to have taken to RML Hospital where he gave his statement that he alongwith Deepak Gupta who was driving the scooty is going back to house, however forgot the way, therefore turned on wrong side at Ashoka Road.
In the meanwhile, one car bearing no. DL 1ZB-5532 driven in rash and negligent manner hit their scooty due to which he/claimant suffered injured in left leg and both the hands.
The driver left the car at the spot and ran away.
Pursuant to his statement, FIR was registered.

sentences.text: 17 . It is well settled that the procedure followed for proceedings conducted by an accident tribunal is similar to that followed by a Civil Court and in Civil matters, the facts are required to be established on preponderance of probabilities and not beyond reasonable doubt, as are required in a criminal prosecution.

Reference in this regard is made to the judgment of Hon'ble Apex Court reported as (2009) 13 SC 530 in Bimla Devi and others Vs. Himachal Road Transport Corporation and others,
wherein it has been observed that strict proof of an accident caused by a particular vehicle in a particular manner may not be possible to be done by the petitioners and the petitioners were merely to establish their case on the touchstone of preponderance of probability.

entities.text: Bimla Devi and others Vs. Himachal Road Transport Corporation and others

sentences.text: 21. In terms of Section 168 of the Motor Vehicle Act, 1988, the compensation which is to be awarded by this Tribunal is required to be 'just'.
In injury cases, a petitioner is entitled to two different kinds of compensation i.e. pecuniary as well as non- pecuniary damages.

The Hon'ble Apex Court in Raj Kumar Vs. Ajay Kumar reported in (2011) 1 SCC 343, has laid down heads under which compensation is awarded in personal injury cases as:-
Pecuniary damages (Special Damages)
(i) Expenses relating to treatment, hospitalization, medicines, transportation,
nourishing food, and miscellaneous expenditure.
(ii) Loss of earnings (and other gains) which the injured would have made had he not been injured, comprising :
(a) Loss of earning during the period of treatment;
(b) Loss of future earnings on account of permanent disability.

Having considered the ratio of aforesaid judgment, the compensation payable to petitioner is assessed hereinafter under the following heads as:-
(i) Medical or Treatment Expenses 23.
As per discharge summary, the injured Anand Kumar has been suffered fracture injuries and remained hospitalized in RML hospital from 29.05.2018 to 12.06.2018.

During hospitalization,
some implants and nailing were inserted.
The injured as per the medical prescriptions on record remained under treatment in RML Hospital July 2019 however not filed any medical treatment paper after July 2019.
Therefore, injured found to be under treatment more than one year due to fracture injuries suffered by accident.

Injured did not file any medical bills except a small bill of Rs.
483/-, however in his statement he stated that he has purchased the implant from outside hospital,
but the bill has been misplaced.

As the injured remained under treatment more than one year,
therefore it can be assumed he might have incurred the expenses of Rs. 1,00,000/-, therefore injured is awarded a sum of Rs. 1,00,000/- towards medical bills.
(ii) Loss of earnings 24.

The injured in his affidavit of evidence stated that he is running a grocery shop at monthly rent of Rs. 12,000/- and was DAR No. 120/19 08.07.2025 Page. 8 of 20 Anand Kumar Vs. Pintu Kumar & Ors.
earning around Rs. 20,000/- per month, however neither given any particulars of the shop nor any income tax return or any other documents to show that he is running the said shop.

Accordingly, a sum of Rs. 61,620/- (Rs. 10,270/- X 6 months) is awarded to injured/Anand Kumar under this head.
(iii) Mental and Physical Shock, Pain and Sufferings & Loss of Amenities 25.
As stated above, the petitioner had suffered grievous injuries in the accident.

Though, it is not possible to exactly compensate him for the shock, pain and sufferings etc. which he had actually suffered because of the above injuries, but an effort has to be made to compensate him for the same Anand Kumar vs Pintu Kumar on 8 July, 2025

Still this Tribunal can very well take note of the requirement of conveyance for petitioner for visiting the hospitals and doctors in connection with his treatment and special diet for his early recovery from the injuries suffered because of the accident.
Considering the facts and circumstances of the present case, an amount of Rs.25,000/- each is being awarded to the petitioner towards special diet and conveyance.

27. Keeping in view the nature of injuries suffered by the claimant, she would have required assistance of some family member/attendant for doing her daily routine work, therefore, a lumsum of Rs.50,000/- is also being awarded to the claimant towards attendant charges.

opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
16. The Hon'ble Apex Court in Mangla Ram Vs. Oriental Insurance Co. Ltd. & Ors., 2018 Law Suit (SC) 303 has observed that filing of charge sheet against the driver prima facie points towards his complicity in driving the vehicle rashly and negligently.
17 . It is well settled that the procedure followed for proceedings conducted by an accident tribunal is similar to that followed by a Civil Court and in Civil matters, the facts are required to be established on preponderance of probabilities and not beyond reasonable doubt, as are required in a criminal prosecution.
As the issue No.1 has been proved in favour of the petitioner, he has become entitled to be compensated for the injuries DAR No. 120/19 08.07.2025 Page. 6 of 20 Anand Kumar Vs. Pintu Kumar & Ors.
suffered by him in the accident, but the computation of compensation and liability to pay the same are required to be decided.
21. In terms of Section 168 of the Motor Vehicle Act, 1988, the compensation which is to be awarded by this Tribunal is required to be 'just'.
In injury cases, a petitioner is entitled to two different kinds of compensation i.e. pecuniary as well as non- pecuniary damages.
Considering the nature of the injury, it can be assumed, he could not work around six months, therefore, the injured/Anand Kumar, is entitled for compensation of minimum wages of unskilled worker for six months.
(iii) Mental and Physical Shock, Pain and Sufferings & Loss of Amenities 25.
Hence, keeping in view the extent and nature of the injuries suffered by the petitioner and duration of the treatment taken by him etc., an amount of Rs.50,000/- each is being awarded to him towards (i) mental and physical shock and (ii) for pain and sufferings respectively.
However, she has not placed on record any document regarding conveyance and special diet.
Still this Tribunal can very well take note of the requirement of conveyance for petitioner for visiting the hospitals and doctors in connection with his treatment and special diet for his early recovery from the injuries suffered because of the accident.
The maturity amount of the FDR (s) on monthly basis net of TDS be credited by Electronic Clearing System (ECS) in the above account of claimant.
No loan, advance or withdrawal or pre-mature discharge be allowed on the MACAD without permission of the Court.
The concerned bank shall not issue any cheque book and/or debit card to claimant(s).
However, in case the debit card and/or cheque book have already been issued, bank shall cancel the same before the disbursement of the award amount.
opennyai_summary.decision:
Considering the facts and circumstances of the present case, an amount of Rs.25,000/- each is being awarded to the petitioner towards special diet and conveyance.
27. Keeping in view the nature of injuries suffered by the claimant, she would have required assistance of some family member/attendant for doing her daily routine work, therefore, a lumsum of Rs.50,000/- is also being awarded to the claimant towards attendant charges.
The petitioner is thus entitled to an amount of Rs.1,00,000/- (Rs.25,000/- + Rs. 25,000 + Rs. 50,000/-) under this head.

1,25,000/- + Rs.1,00,000/-) along with 7.5% interest from the date of filing of DAR.

All the respondents are though being held jointly and severally liable to pay the awarded amount of compensation to claimant, but respondent no.3 being insurer of offending vehicle, is directed to deposit the award amount with UCO Bank, Patiala House Court Branch, along with interest @ 7.5%
per annum from the date of filing of DAR by RTGS/NEFT/IMPS in bank account being maintained in the above said bank in name of this tribunal within 30 days from today, failing which it is liable to pay interest at the rate of 9% per annum for the period of delay.

that event, in light of judgment of the Hon'ble High Court of Delhi passed in the case of New India Assurance Company Limited Vs. Kashmiri Lal 2007 ACJ 688, this compensation shall be recovered by attaching the bank account of respondent no. 3 with a cost of Rs.5,000/-.
